questions.note: Order is right: hallux longest, toe 2 about 9 mm back at the tip (plantar, ~20 px/mm), 3–4 descending. Toe 2 now has a PIP knuckle (~16.7 mm), a waist (~12.8) and a pulp bulb (~15.4) at 47.6 px/mm. Against that: the hallux is ~31 mm wide but ~21 mm deep (front 21.7, medial 17.9 px/mm), the knuckle wrinkles are one stamp, a cuff ledge rings toe 2 below and no toe-base creases.

Hallux plate 19.3 mm and toe 2 ~10 mm wide (front, 21.7 px/mm), in range; the bed now shows pink and highlights are soft. But each plate is a tile in an even gutter with one rim, the free edges are constant-width white French tips with a grey cut face, the lunula is a straight-edged wedge, two pale bands stack at the tip, and toe 2's edge shows glassy from below.

Nothing in frame reads as tendon: no EHL cord over the first MTP onto the hallux, no extensor slip to toe 2, no veins; the dorsal profile in the medial view is a smooth line. The only raised line on the first MTP is a scar-like arc. The saphenous vein is out of frame and not judged.

No glow: toe shadow sides stay clearly darker and thin tips do not turn red. Micro-relief is present at about the right scale (dorsal cells ~0.2–0.6 mm at 98 px/mm, plantar ridges ~0.45 mm pitch at 20 px/mm) but wrong in kind: crumpled-foil facets in highlights, corduroy stripes through creases, smear in the web shadow. Colour and sheen not marked down (first-pass material).

defects.what: The hallux plate is a flat rounded-rectangle tile set in an even, narrow gutter with one thin uniform rim on its medial, proximal and lateral sides; every edge is exposed, so it reads as a press-on nail.
defects.fix: Roll the lateral folds about 1 mm over the plate's sides so they hide its edges, make the proximal fold a 1.5 mm cushion with a 0.4 mm eponychium, and let the plate curve down into the lateral grooves.

defects.what: Both free edges, hallux and toe 2, are constant-width opaque white bands with a smooth grey cut face and no grime line beneath: an acrylic French tip, not a clipped toenail.
defects.fix: A clipped edge varies in width, is faintly yellow-grey and opaque, shows small clipper facets at the corners and a thin dark under-edge grime line (#6d5a4a at 25 %).

defects.what: In profile the hallux is ~21 mm deep at the IP and ~18.5 mm at the nail root (17.9 px/mm) yet ~31 mm wide in the front view (21.7 px/mm): a 1.5:1 flattened section, broadened without the depth Jeff's direction pairs with it (~25 mm).
defects.fix: Add 3–4 mm of depth, mostly as plantar pulp volume under the distal phalanx, so the section stays near round as the toe was widened.

defects.what: The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP carry the same 3–4 long, evenly spaced, parallel glossy grooves spanning the joint, which dent the dorsal profile like bellows in the medial view.
defects.fix: Knuckle skin shows a loose oval cluster of short, broken, branching wrinkles of mixed depth (about 0.2 mm, 1 mm pitch) with finer lines between; none spans the toe or dents the silhouette.

defects.what: Under toe 2 a straight, crisp ledge with a white glint rings the toe at the PIP; the proximal segment flares at its ends and is smooth, the distal one narrower and ridged, like a sleeve cuff.
defects.fix: A plantar PIP crease is a soft fold about 0.5 mm deep with the same skin level and ridging on both sides, the ridges turning to run along it.

defects.what: No EHL cord runs over the first MTP onto the hallux and no extensor slip reaches toe 2; the dorsum in frame is a smooth dome with an oily sheen and no veins.
defects.fix: Raise the EHL as a 1–1.5 mm cord along the first ray onto the hallux and soft EDL/EDB slips to toe 2 that catch the rim light, fading only over the toes.

defects.what: A thin raised glossy arc crosses the first MTP dorsum and notches the medial profile, reading as a healed bunionectomy scar.
defects.fix: Over the first MTP only faint, broken transverse wrinkles show; no continuous raised line.

defects.what: The 1–2 web ends in a straight horizontal margin meeting toe 2's medial wall at a near-right angle: a shelf spanning the toes.
defects.fix: The commissure is a soft U, lowest mid-cleft, rising in concave fillets up each toe's side, its skin finely wrinkled.

defects.what: Friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one angle across the ball, the hallux pad and toe 2 and up the medial side, running straight through the creases like corduroy; no whorl or loop on the hallux pad.
defects.fix: Ridges follow each pad's dome in a whorl or loop, run transversely across the ball, break and turn at every flexion crease, and fade up the sides.

defects.what: From below the hallux, and toe 2 beside it, grow straight out of the ball with no digito-plantar crease at their base, so the toes have no root.
defects.fix: A deep curved fold separates each toe pad from the ball under the MTP heads, deepest under the hallux, with the toe's proximal pad bulging distal to it.

defects.what: The hallux lunula is a white wedge with a straight distal border, thickest at the medial corner and fading laterally, not a centred half-moon.
defects.fix: A ~3.5 mm crescent centred on the nail axis with a soft convex distal border, its sides tucked under the proximal fold.

defects.what: Behind the free edge a second pale wavy band runs parallel to it, split off by a thin red line, so the tip reads as two lacquer layers or distal onycholysis.
defects.fix: The pink bed ends at one narrow onychodermal band, slightly darker and amber-pink, then the opaque free edge.

defects.what: Toe 2's DIP crease is one long even groove with a lit lip across about two-thirds of the toe: a knife cut.
defects.fix: Two or three short, soft, slightly oblique creases, shallow at their ends, with fine wrinkles between.

defects.what: From below, toe 2's free edge shows past its pulp as a clear glassy rim with a bright corner, and the hallux's free-edge corners glint past its pulp.
defects.fix: From below the pulp hides a trimmed free edge; at most a dull opaque edge shows at the tip of a curled toe.

defects.what: The hallux's proximal phalanx, like toe 2, carries no hair at all, where §3.4 asks for an 8–12 hair tuft on the hallux and 2–4 hairs on toe 2, as most men's toes and the anchor feet show.
defects.fix: 8–12 dark hairs 5–8 mm long lying flat distally on a 12 × 10 mm patch of the hallux proximal phalanx; 2–4 of 3–6 mm on toe 2.

defects.what: In highlights the dorsal micro-relief breaks into sharp angular facets like crumpled cellophane, and the same dark-outlined crackle covers the toe and web dorsum evenly.
defects.fix: Skin's network is soft furrows round slightly domed plateaus, longer directional primary lines with finer secondary ones; highlights break along furrows, never into facets.

defects.what: In clay a tiny bright fleck sits in the pocket under the hallux free edge, as if the plate's underside pokes through the hyponychium.
defects.fix: The hyponychium seals under the free edge; no part of the plate shows through skin.

defects.what: At the zoom the free edge's lateral corner is a squared slab end sitting on the pulp, its cut face a uniform grey band; the medial corner is the same.
defects.fix: A trimmed corner is slightly rounded and dips into the lateral groove, its cut face uneven and opaque like the plate.

defects.what: In clay a crisp line runs down toe 2's medial wall where the 1–2 web joins it, a pinched fold or seam instead of a smooth fillet.
defects.fix: Web skin flows into the toe's side in a smooth concave fillet with no line.

defects.what: In the web zoom the shadowed recess breaks into soft blotches and loses its micro-relief, like denoiser smear.
defects.fix: Shadowed web skin keeps its fine wrinkles and furrows; render this closeup with enough samples that the denoiser does not smear them.

ranked: [D1] The hallux nail, the focus of most views, is a press-on: a flat rounded-rectangle tile in an even gutter with one thin rim on three sides, every edge exposed; real lateral folds roll over the plate's sides and the plate curves down under them.

[D2] Both free edges are constant-width opaque white bands with a smooth grey cut face and no grime: an acrylic French tip. A clipped toenail edge is uneven, faintly yellow-grey, a little faceted by the clippers, with a thin dark line under it.
[D3] The hallux is about 31 mm wide but only about 21 mm deep at the IP and 18.5 at the nail root: widened without the matching depth, so it reads broad and flat rather than round.

[D4] The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wear one stamp: three or four long, evenly spaced, parallel glossy grooves spanning the joint and denting the profile like bellows; real knuckle skin has short, broken, branching wrinkles of mixed depth.

[D6] No EHL cord over the first MTP onto the hallux and no extensor slip to toe 2: a lean 40-year-old's forefoot shows them as soft ridges catching the light, as the anchor feet do; here it is a smooth dome.
[D5] Under toe 2 a straight crisp ledge with a white glint rings the toe at the PIP, smooth and flared above, narrower and ridged below: a sleeve cuff that skin cannot make.
[D7] A thin raised glossy arc crosses the first MTP dorsum and notches the medial profile; a podiatrist reads a healed bunionectomy scar.

[D9] Plantar ridges are straight parallel stripes at one angle over the ball, both pads and up the medial side, running through creases like corduroy; the hallux pad should carry a whorl or loop, and ridges break at creases.
[D10] From below, the hallux and toe 2 grow straight out of the ball with no digito-plantar crease, so they have no root; a real sole folds deeply where each toe pad meets the ball.
[D8] The 1–2 web ends in a straight horizontal margin meeting toe 2's wall at a near-right angle, a shelf between the toes; a real commissure is a soft U rising in concave fillets up each toe.
[D15] The hallux and toe 2 are bald; most men's big toes carry a small tuft of dark hairs on the proximal phalanx, as §3.4 asks and the anchor feet show.
[D11] The hallux lunula is a white wedge with a straight distal border, thickest at the medial corner, not a centred half-moon with a soft convex edge.
[D14] From below, toe 2's free edge shows past the pulp as a clear glassy rim with a bright corner, and the hallux's corners glint past its pulp; the pulp should hide a trimmed edge.
[D13] Toe 2's DIP crease is one long even groove with a lit lip across two-thirds of the toe, a knife cut rather than two or three short soft creases.
[D12] Behind the free edge a second pale wavy band parallels it, split off by a thin red line: two lacquer layers, or onycholysis, instead of one narrow onychodermal band.
The toes read young and pedicured rather than a 40-year-old boot-wearer's: unlined skin between stamped creases, manicured nails with no thickening, ridging, yellowing or grime.

[D16] Dorsal micro-relief is one dark-outlined crackle, and in highlights it breaks into sharp facets like crumpled cellophane; skin's network is soft furrows round domed plateaus with longer directional primary lines.
[D18] At the zoom the free-edge corners are squared slab ends resting on the pulp with a uniform grey cut face; a trimmed corner is slightly rounded and dips into the lateral groove.
The first-pass skin's oily sheen on the forefoot and toe 2's knuckle reads as vinyl and would flatten the low relief tendons need (declared, noted only for what it hides).
[D19] In clay a crisp line runs down toe 2's medial wall where the web joins it, a pinched fold or seam, not a smooth fillet.
[D17] In clay a tiny bright fleck sits in the pocket under the hallux free edge, as if the plate pokes through the hyponychium.
[D20] In the web zoom the shadowed recess breaks into soft blotches with no micro-relief, like denoiser smear, so the web skin goes waxy where it should be finely wrinkled.
